condition.required_scene: A visible lever is linked to a door, bridge, lift, or machine that changes state.

candidates.example_sentence: The child pulled the old lever, and the secret door opened.
positive_visual_cues: The hand visibly grips a lever handle.
The lever rotates or travels to a new angle while the body leans into the pull.
The linked door, bridge, or mechanism changes state in the same shot.
negative_cues: Pulling empty air or an invisible rope.
A door handle moves without a distinct lever.
The character strains but no prop or linked state changes.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Find the lever, look at the linked device, and place the hand on the handle.
four_phase_contract.act: Pull the handle through a clear arc until the lever reaches its end position.
four_phase_contract.hold: Keep the lowered lever and the newly opened or moved device visible together.
four_phase_contract.recover: Release the handle, return the hand to neutral, and look toward the result.

condition.required_scene: A marked dial has a visible starting symbol and a visible target mark or alignment.

candidates.example_sentence: Mina turned the golden dial until the moon symbol faced up.
positive_visual_cues: Fingers hold the rim of a marked circular dial.
The dial rotates around its own center while the character stays grounded.
The target symbol stops aligned with a fixed indicator.
negative_cues: The whole character rotates instead of the prop.
A key enters a lock, which is turn_key rather than a dial.
The dial jumps between symbols without continuous contact.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Inspect the starting symbol and the fixed target mark, then place fingers on the dial rim.
four_phase_contract.act: Rotate the dial in a visible circular arc through one or more marked positions.
four_phase_contract.hold: Keep the target symbol aligned with the fixed indicator.
four_phase_contract.recover: Release the dial and look at the unlocked or activated device.

condition.required_scene: A hand-held gem and a matching socket, crown, altar, or stone are both visible.

candidates.example_sentence: The princess placed the blue gem in the crown-shaped stone.
positive_visual_cues: The gem is visibly held above a matching recess.
The gem leaves the hand and settles into the socket.
The gem remains fixed and the artifact may glow only after contact.
negative_cues: A gem floats while still attached to the hand.
There is no socket or receiving surface.
The object disappears without a visible placement result.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Compare the gem with the visible socket and align the hand above it.
four_phase_contract.act: Lower the gem into the recess until the hand can release it.
four_phase_contract.hold: Show the gem fixed in the socket and the completed artifact state.
four_phase_contract.recover: Withdraw the hand and look at the activated or completed object.

condition.required_scene: The bridge entrance, traversable span, and opposite ground are visible on one path axis.

candidates.example_sentence: The child crosses the old bridge to reach the castle.
positive_visual_cues: Feet move from the near bank onto the bridge surface.
The character traverses the span with the gap or water below visible.
Both feet reach the opposite ground before recovery.
negative_cues: Walking on flat ground with no bridge endpoints.
A jump over a gap with both feet leaving the bridge path.
The character climbs the bridge rail instead of crossing it.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Face the bridge entrance, check the far side, and align both feet with the span.
four_phase_contract.act: Take careful steps along the bridge while the bridge and gap remain visible.
four_phase_contract.hold: Show the character mid-span with one foot placed on the bridge and the far side ahead.
four_phase_contract.recover: Step onto the opposite ground, leave the bridge, and stabilize.

condition.required_scene: Two close boundaries form a narrow gap with a visible far-side exit.

candidates.example_sentence: The child squeezes through the crack in the ruined wall and finds a secret passage.
positive_visual_cues: The character turns the shoulders sideways before entering the gap.
The arms and torso compress between two visible walls or rocks.
The full body emerges on the far side and the shoulders expand again.
negative_cues: Four-limbed crawling on an open floor.
Stopping behind a cover without crossing the gap.
The character vanishes without boundary contact or an exit reveal.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Inspect the gap width, turn the body sideways, and draw the shoulders inward.
four_phase_contract.act: Press one foot at a time through the narrow opening while keeping contact with the boundaries.
four_phase_contract.hold: Maintain the compressed torso at the middle of the gap with both boundaries readable.
four_phase_contract.recover: Clear the far side, straighten the shoulders, and return to a stable stance.

condition.required_scene: A low branch, beam, fallen tree, or gate creates a passable space below it.

candidates.example_sentence: The child ducks under the fallen tree in the forest.
positive_visual_cues: The character looks at a low obstacle and lowers head and shoulders.
The body travels beneath the obstacle while the feet keep moving.
The character rises only after clearing the obstacle.
negative_cues: A stationary crouch with no obstacle or forward passage.
A bow in open space without a height constraint.
Hands and knees touch the ground as in crawling.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Notice the low obstacle, slow the feet, and release the knees.
four_phase_contract.act: Lower the head and shoulders and pass forward beneath the obstacle.
four_phase_contract.hold: Keep the character at the lowest point under the obstacle with the obstacle visibly overhead.
four_phase_contract.recover: Clear the obstacle, raise the body, and resume a stable path stance.

condition.required_scene: A closed door or other vertical surface is directly in front of the character.

candidates.example_sentence: The little knight knocked on the castle door three times.
positive_visual_cues: A closed door remains fixed in front of the character.
A closed fist contacts the same door area repeatedly.
The hand lowers and the character waits before the door changes state.
negative_cues: Knocking empty air.
A single push that opens the door immediately.
A large weapon swing or side-to-side wave.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Face the closed door, raise a closed hand, and choose the contact point.
four_phase_contract.act: Tap the same door area three clear times with the fist.
four_phase_contract.hold: Lower the hand and wait while the closed door remains visible.
four_phase_contract.recover: Turn toward the opening door or return to neutral after the response.

condition.required_scene: A distinct seal or stamp and wax, clay, or marked surface are visible together.

candidates.example_sentence: The wizard pressed the star seal onto the red wax.
positive_visual_cues: The seal is held above the wax or receiving surface.
The seal moves vertically into firm surface contact.
A star or other mark remains after the seal is lifted.
negative_cues: A finger pressing an invisible button.
No seal, wax, or lasting surface mark.
A floating magic symbol with no object contact.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Align the seal face with the visible wax or surface.
four_phase_contract.act: Press the seal straight down until it contacts the surface.
four_phase_contract.hold: Keep pressure briefly and show the imprint forming.
four_phase_contract.recover: Lift the seal and reveal the completed mark.

condition.required_scene: A lantern with a visible wick and a separate flame source is present in a dim setting.

candidates.example_sentence: The girl lit the lantern, and the dark cave became bright.
positive_visual_cues: The flame source approaches and touches the wick.
The flame remains attached to the lantern rather than the hand.
The lantern and nearby cave visibly become the stable light source.
negative_cues: Light emitted from an empty hand.
A flame that floats separately from the wick.
No change in the lantern or surrounding illumination.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Bring the flame source to the lantern and locate the wick.
four_phase_contract.act: Touch the flame source to the wick until a small flame appears.
four_phase_contract.hold: Keep the flame on the wick and the lantern illuminating the nearby space.
four_phase_contract.recover: Remove the flame source and hold or set down the lit lantern.

condition.required_scene: Shallow water has a visible waterline, resistance, ripples, and a dry bank for recovery.

candidates.example_sentence: The child wades across the shallow stream to the hidden cave.
positive_visual_cues: The waterline crosses the lower legs while the torso stays upright.
Short heavy steps displace water and create ripples.
The character reaches dry ground and shakes off or stabilizes.
negative_cues: Walking on a dry floor.
A horizontal body and arm strokes of swimming.
Diving into water or walking on top of the surface.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Check the shallow water and place the first foot into it.
four_phase_contract.act: Push through the water with short steps while ripples follow the legs.
four_phase_contract.hold: Keep one leg raised against visible water resistance with the waterline stable.
four_phase_contract.recover: Step onto the dry bank, clear the water, and regain neutral balance.

condition.required_scene: The character sits or kneels in a boat, holds an oar, contacts water, and the boat moves.

candidates.example_sentence: The child rows across the moonlit lake toward the castle.
positive_visual_cues: Both hands grip an oar with the blade entering the water.
The body pulls the oar through a repeatable stroke.
The boat changes position relative to the water or shore.
negative_cues: Arm waving without an oar or boat.
Swimming with the body in the water.
A stationary boat with no water contact or displacement.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Grip the oar in the boat and aim the blade toward the water.
four_phase_contract.act: Place the blade in the water and pull it toward the body.
four_phase_contract.hold: Show the oar in the water while the boat advances against the surface.
four_phase_contract.recover: Lift the blade clear, reset the hands, and prepare the next stroke.

condition.required_scene: Two visible characters face each other with enough room for hand contact and a short shake.

candidates.example_sentence: The two young travelers shook hands when they reached the castle gate.
positive_visual_cues: The two characters approach and extend corresponding hands.
Hands visibly meet and remain joined for a short vertical shake.
Both characters release and face each other in a stable hold.
negative_cues: One character offers a hand but no contact occurs.
Side-to-side waving without a partner hand.
An object passes between the hands.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Place the two characters face to face and extend their hands toward the same point.
four_phase_contract.act: Make the hands contact and close into a shared grip.
four_phase_contract.hold: Perform one or two short up-and-down shakes while maintaining the hand contact.
four_phase_contract.recover: Release the grip and return both characters to a relaxed facing stance.

condition.required_scene: A visible person or animal is positioned as the receiver and can respond by approaching.

candidates.example_sentence: The fairy beckoned the child to come closer to the lantern.
positive_visual_cues: The signaling character fixes the gaze on a visible receiver.
The palm faces inward and the fingers repeat a clear come-here motion.
The receiver begins to approach or visibly acknowledges the signal.
negative_cues: Side-to-side waving with no invitation direction.
Pointing at a location without an inward hand path.
Hand motion in empty space with no receiver.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Find the visible receiver, orient the torso toward it, and raise the signaling hand.
four_phase_contract.act: Curl the palm or fingers inward twice to invite the receiver closer.
four_phase_contract.hold: Keep the receiver in view and maintain the invitation gaze after the signal.
four_phase_contract.recover: Lower the hand as the receiver approaches or the scene transitions.

condition.required_scene: A visible threat or frightening event is placed on the gaze axis and remains identifiable.

candidates.example_sentence: The little fox cowered behind the stone when the dragon roared.
positive_visual_cues: The character keeps looking toward the visible threat.
The body lowers while taking one or two steps backward.
Arms protect the chest or head without fully disappearing behind cover.
negative_cues: A neutral crouch with no threat or backward movement.
A one-frame shoulder flinch.
The character vanishes behind a cover as in hiding.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Face the threat and begin raising the shoulders in fear.
four_phase_contract.act: Lower the body, retreat slightly, and raise protective arms.
four_phase_contract.hold: Maintain the low protective posture while keeping the threat in the gaze axis.
four_phase_contract.recover: After the threat passes, raise the head and return slowly to neutral.

condition.required_scene: Two characters enter the same place, face each other, and stop close enough for a relationship event.

candidates.example_sentence: The child met a friendly fox at the edge of the enchanted forest.
positive_visual_cues: Two roots approach from different sides or routes.
They share the same location and face each other in a mutual hold.
The scene leaves room for the next handshake, conversation, or shared journey.
negative_cues: One character merely follows another.
The characters pass without stopping or facing each other.
Only one character is present.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Place both characters at separate approach points with their attention oriented toward one another.
four_phase_contract.act: Move both characters toward the shared meeting point.
four_phase_contract.hold: Stop both characters in the same location and show mutual facing and eye-line.
four_phase_contract.recover: Leave them in a neutral relationship pose ready for the next story beat.

condition.required_scene: A private speaker is separated by a door, wall, window, or other cover, and the listener remains partly concealed.

candidates.example_sentence: The princess eavesdropped outside the wizard's door.
positive_visual_cues: The speaker's face or mouth is visible on the far side of a cover.
The listener places the ear and one side of the face close to the boundary while most of the body stays hidden.
The listener withdraws quickly after the private exchange.
negative_cues: Open public listening with no cover or private speaker.
A hand placed on the ear with no spatial relationship.
Full-body peeking without an identifiable conversation.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Notice the covered speaker area and move beside the door, wall, or window.
four_phase_contract.act: Lean the ear and face toward the boundary while keeping most of the body concealed.
four_phase_contract.hold: Maintain the hidden listening position with the speaker and cover visible in the composite scene.
four_phase_contract.recover: Pull the head back, leave the cover, and return to a neutral path or hiding position.

condition.required_scene: A hard-to-see person or object has a defined position and appears at a known discovery moment.

candidates.example_sentence: At last, Hana spotted the silver key under the leaf.
positive_visual_cues: The character searches before the hidden target becomes visible.
The head and gaze make one sharp switch toward the target.
The discovery hold leads to pointing, approaching, or picking up the target.
negative_cues: Continuous broad scanning with no discovery moment.
A pointing gesture without a hidden target.
The target position or reveal timing is not specified.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Search the defined area while the target remains hidden or unnoticed.
four_phase_contract.act: At the reveal moment, stop the gaze and orient the head and torso toward the target.
four_phase_contract.hold: Keep the target and the newly fixed discovery gaze visible together.
four_phase_contract.recover: Begin the next action toward the target or return the hands to neutral.

condition.required_scene: A visible door, bridge, choice, or tool is approached but must not change state during the hesitation.

candidates.example_sentence: Mina hesitated before opening the dark castle door.
positive_visual_cues: The character approaches a specific goal and raises a hand toward it.
The hand stops short or pauses before contact, with a visible incomplete state.
The hand withdraws and the body makes a small retreat or turns toward another choice.
negative_cues: A completed opening, unlocking, or pressing action.
Standing still with no goal or unfinished approach.
Cowering or hiding behind a cover instead of making an incomplete attempt.

four_phase_contract.prepare: Approach the visible goal and prepare the hand or foot for the intended action.
four_phase_contract.act: Move toward the contact point, then stop just before changing the target state.
four_phase_contract.hold: Keep the unfinished reach and uncertain gaze for a short readable pause.
four_phase_contract.recover: Withdraw the hand, step back, or turn toward an alternative path without completing the goal.

rejected.reason: Requires long prop continuity and screen travel; otherwise reads as hold, lift, pick_up, or journey.
Tiny-object release and landing are fragile at small scale and can read as fall or throw.
Liquid and vessel effects carry the meaning and need a later effects composite.
A continuous liquid stream between two vessels is hard to preserve in a general motion sheet.
Sheath occlusion, weapon safety, and combat adjacency make it production-specific.
Silent playback cannot rely on sound and rope variants resemble pull_lever or wave.
The decisive evidence is a tiny written mark and readable map content.
Same seal, surface, and imprint as press_seal; only timing differs.
Without an explicit hand-planted obstacle it is an embellished jump; with one it needs a later safety test.
Lighting, occlusion, and camera reveal carry more meaning than the character motion.
Vehicle type, step height, and camera placement vary too much for one stable action.
The reverse vehicle transition is equally vehicle- and camera-specific.
Needs route history or markers; body motion alone is ordinary journey.
Choosing a longer route is scene/map information rather than a stable body motion.
Without a visible threat it is backward journey; the threat relation belongs in scene metadata.
Repeated torso contractions are too close to the implemented sneeze at low resolution.
Controlled collapse overlaps fall_roll and has a high safety/grounding risk.
Needs an initiating event and reads as a short reaction close to stagger.
Needs an initiating threat and is visually indistinguishable from stop without context.
Hand-together stillness is close to sit, pray, and magic and needs belief context.
Hand-together posture is not enough to distinguish it from magic or other posture scenes.
Emotion and facial effects dominate; no stable action silhouette passes silently.
Without audio or an audience it is hard to distinguish from talking.
Audio is the decisive cue; an empty-mouth body sheet is not reliable.
Micro vibration is too small and overlaps fear/freeze state cues.
Natural blink is not a reliable canonical action without a light or target scene.
Needs a clear cover and target or collapses into hide or investigate; already reviewed.
Needs sound direction or a speaker; the hand-to-ear pose is not sufficiently distinct.
The difference from eavesdrop is event timing and accident, which needs editing/audio context.
Needs a partner, ear proximity, and speech context; preserve as a scene label.
Continuous partner hand contact overlaps hug/generic hold and needs two-person tracking.
Requires a protected target and a threat direction; build as a composite scene first.
Requires a moving target and a timed hand contact; static props read as grasp or pick_up.
Requires a restraint and a target that becomes free; object-only release can read as drop.
Requires an opponent or threat plus a weapon or authority relationship.
Needs visible face and a revealed target; otherwise it is only a surprise emotion.
Needs a visible pain source and face resolution; otherwise it is flinch.
Face micro-change needs a small target or bright light and a medium close view.
Needs a listener and a nearby sound/risk; finger-to-lips alone is ambiguous.
Alternating speech and conflict require two characters, voice, and before/after context.
Its meaning is the before/after relationship change, not one stable pose.
A bowed head without the wronged partner and cause is just bow.
Already represented by the Round 3 generated cycle and conflicts with the old investigate-like pose.
